newsitem.title: GREECE: GUARANTEE FUND BOARD MAY RESIGN OVER DRAFT BILL.
newsitem.headline: GUARANTEE FUND BOARD MAY RESIGN OVER DRAFT BILL.

text.p: Four of the five members of the board of directors of the Athens bourse's guarantee fund were likely to resign on Friday, official sources said.

The four, including all members except bourse president Manolis Xanthakis, were planning to resign over a national economy draft bill that appears to try to sidestep a recent compromise deal between brokers and the government.

The four, all brokers, were in disagreement over an article of the draft bill that appear to allow the clearing house to avoid paying its part of a 2.6 billion drachma default by Delta Securities, the sources told Reuters.

"There is an effort to have the clearing house avoid assuming its responsibilities and bear its cost as was agreed recently between the brokers association and national economy minister Yannos Papandoniou," one source said.

On Wednesday broker Isaac Mordechai, managing director of ABN AMRO Axias Securities resigned from the exchange's guarantee fund board citing personal reasons. He was replaced by broker Thanasis Halkiadis.
On Tuesday Papandoniou announced a series of measures aimed at a compromise with the brokers association which was refusing to resume trade and blasting the government for a cover up.
His ministry said in a statement that the bourse's clearing house would cover 1.3 billion drachmas of Delta's default and would submit immediate payment to state National Bank .
The clearing house would in turn be entitled to claim the funds it will pay from member Delta Securities and in case the Delta is unable to come up with the funds from the exchange's guarantee fund.

But in a draft bill released to the press on Friday, article A, paragraph two states that "...the guarantee fund must 'submit funds immediately' to the clearing house and this sources say has the brokers on the guarantee fund board going ballistic.

"The resignation of the board members will halt any decision making and consequently no payment on the 1.3 billion drachmas can be made to the clearing house. This leads us to a new interim deadlock," sources said.
The brokers association (SMEHA) will retain legal experts on the civil and penal code to advise it on further action. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
